newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to keep cooperating with U.S. on forex--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to keep cooperating with U.S. on forex--MOF.

text.p: Japan will continue to cooperate with the United States in seeking stability in foreign exchange markets, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said in a statement issued on Tuesday.

The statement, issued after comments by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in New York on Monday about potential sales of U.S. Treasuries by Japan, said Hashimoto regretted that his intentions had not been accurately conveyed.
Reports of his comments caused turmoil in U.S. financial markets late on Monday.

The statement, issued in both Japanese and English, said Hashimoto had been asked whether it would be profitable for the government of Japan and Japanese investors to continue to hold U.S. Treasury bills.

"In response to this question, the prime minister stated that even though some mentions were made of these temptations in the past, Japan never sold Treasury bonds for profits because of the over-riding importance we attach to (the) Japan-U.S. relationship and to the stability of the currency market," it said.
The statement, issued under the name of Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Takatoshi Kato and dated June 23, said Hashimoto had instructed Kato to make the following comments:
"1. The prime minister regrets that his intention was not accurately conveyed.
2. The prime minister's intention is to maintain the consistent policy of the government of Japan, which has been implemented, bearing in mind the good relations between Japan and the U.S.
3. The Japanese authorities will continue to cooperate with the U.S. with a view to maintaining stable foreign exchange markets."
